adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, in `handleNewBooking.ts`, builds multi-host destination calendars for COLLECTIVE team events (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`). However, when persisting the booking it only connects the first destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so the booking record retains only one destination calendar. Later flows that reconstruct `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar`/`user.destinationCalendar` (e.g., `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`) can only ever rebuild a single-element array, losing the additional hosts’ destination calendars. That means subsequent operations that rely on `evt.destinationCalendar` (not just references) cannot “see” the other hosts’ calendars, which is inconsistent with the new multi-destination behavior introduced here.
